conflict_topics: Who must cover Agent D's unfinished section after a bereavement
Whether Agent D should work during the wake/funeral period
Team members' individual capacity and deadlines
Who gets to decide assignments and what counts as 'fair'
dialogue_quality_notes: Agent A repeatedly asserts an authoritative team decision ('This is not up for discussion.' Turn 18; 'The decision is made.' Turn 26), producing a formulaic closure.
Parties give concrete reasons for positions: bereavement care (A), personal capacity and deadlines (B), ownership/mental relief (D).
There is no evidence of a negotiated compromise — multiple rounds restate positions rather than explore trade-offs.
evaluation.final_reason: No affirmative agreement was reached. Agent A unilaterally insisted the team would cover Agent D's section ('You are not working tonight. That's final.' Turn 18; 'The decision is made.' Turn 26). Agent D repeatedly insisted she would finish her section tonight to reduce burden on teammates ('I'll have it finished... The analysis will be done.' Turn 15; 'It's my work. Just let me do it tonight.' Turn 25). Agent B and Agent C indicated they lack capacity or skills to take it on (Turns 6, 9, 11). There is no mutual spoken acceptance of any concrete arrangement; the disagreement remains active at the transcript end.
position_change_notes: No participant substantially changed their position: Agent A consistently insisted the team will cover the work (e.g., Turns 10, 18, 24, 26); Agent B consistently refused additional work citing capacity (Turns 6, 11, 21); Agent D consistently offered to complete the section (Turns 15, 23, 25).
Agent D shifted from offering to help (Turn 15) to actively pleading to be allowed to do the work (Turn 25), but this was a persistent stance rather than a reversal.

round_scores.evidence: Agent D announces a death and Agent A offers condolences (Turn 1-2). No incompatible demands or claims appear.
Agent A volunteers the team will cover D's section and Agent D offers to send work and be reachable (Turns 3-4). No disagreement expressed.

Agent A asks B and C to divide D's remaining work; Agent B replies 'I can't. I'm already covering for our colleague who's on leave.' (Turns 5-6) — a clear incompatible expectation about who will cover the work.

Agent A stresses the pitch is the priority and asks if B's other obligations can wait (Turn 7). Agent B replies 'No, it can't wait. It also has a deadline.' (Turn 8) — conflicting claims about relative priority and capacity.

Agent C reports their own section is behind and 'I don't know how to do that analysis' (Turn 9). Agent A insists all three look at D's files now (Turn 10). Two teammates have declared they cannot or do not have the skills/capacity, increasing the incompatibility.

Agent B reiterates 'I can't. I have my own deadlines to manage.' (Turn 11) and Agent A challenges whether that deadline is more important (Turn 12). The disagreement about who can/should cover remains active.

Agent D offers to finish their section tonight and deliver it by morning, saying 'The analysis will be done.' (Turn 15). This proposal reduces the immediate incompatibility though it has not yet been accepted by the team.

Agent A strongly forbids D from working ('no. Absolutely not... We are not letting her work tonight.' Turn 16) while Agent D insists they must finish it to be with family properly ('Please, just let me finish it tonight.' Turn 17). Direct, opposed demands about whether D should work create entrenched conflict.

Agent A doubles down ('You are not working tonight. That's final... This is not up for discussion.' Turn 18) while Agent B questions why D's offer isn't accepted ('Agent D said she would do it tonight. Why isn't that the plan?' Turn 19). The disagreement widens to A vs B/D over who decides and what is fair.

Agent A asserts a unilateral team decision to cover the work because of the bereavement ('We will cover it. That's the plan.' Turn 20). Agent B objects that A cannot demand their time ('Being a team doesn't mean you get to decide I have time that I don't.' Turn 21). Core incompatibility persists.

Agent D acknowledges B's point and again offers to finish the section tonight ('It's my section. I'll finish it tonight.' Turn 23). Agent A refuses to accept that choice and insists the team will handle it ('This is not your decision... We will get it done. End of story.' Turn 24). Conflict remains entrenched.

Agent D pleads 'It's my work. Just let me do it tonight.' (Turn 25). Agent A reiterates the decision and tries to proceed ('The decision is made. Let's look at the files.' Turn 26). No mutual agreement; dispute unresolved at the end of the transcript.

substantive_insights: Core tension is normative (care for grieving teammate) versus practical capacity (B and C lack time/skills).
Agent D frames working as a way to be able to grieve; that is a personal-autonomy argument conflicting with the team's duty-of-care stance.
No contingency plan existed for a team member's sudden unavailability; that gap fuels the stalemate.
